chunks: 1. ʿAlī ibn Ḥātim, from Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, said:

I wrote to him, peace be upon him: May I be your ransom, sometimes the الهلال becomes obscured from us in the month of Ramadan, then on the following day we see the الهلال before midday, and sometimes we see it after midday. Do you hold that we should break the fast before midday when we see it, or not? And how do you instruct me regarding that? So he, peace be upon him, wrote: Complete it until night, for if it were complete, it would have been seen before midday.

2. From him, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, from his father, from al-Ḥusayn, from Yūsuf ibn ʿAqīl, from Muḥammad ibn Qays, from Abī Jaʿfar, peace be upon him, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn, peace be upon him, said:

When you see the الهلال, then break the fast, or a just one from among the Muslims bears witness to it. But if you do not see the الهلال except from the middle of the day or its end, then complete the fasting until night. And if it is obscured from you, then count thirty and then break the fast.
3. Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd, from al-Qāsim ibn Sulaymān, from Jarrāḥ al-Madāʾinī, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh, peace be upon him, said:
Whoever sees the الهلال of Shawwāl by day during Ramadan should complete his fasting.

4. And from him, from Faḍālah, from Abān ibn ʿUthmān, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh, peace be upon him, about the الهلال of Ramadan becoming obscured from us on the twenty-ninth of Shaʿbān, and he said:

Do not fast it unless you see it. If the people of another town testify that they saw it, then make it up. And if you see it in the middle of the day, then complete your fast until night—meaning, complete your fast until night on the basis that it is from Shaʿbān, without intending that it is from Ramadan.
5. As for what Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb narrated, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh, peace be upon him, who said:
If they see the الهلال before midday, then it belongs to the previous night; and if they see it after midday, then it belongs to the coming night.

6. And what Saʿd ibn ʿAbdillāh narrated, from Abī Jaʿfar, from Abī Ṭālib ʿAbdillāh ibn al-Ṣalt, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿUbayd ibn Zurārah and ʿAbdillāh ibn Bukayr, who both said: Abū ʿAbdillāh, peace be upon him, said:
If the الهلال is seen before midday, then that day is from Shawwāl; and if it is seen after midday, then it is from the month of Ramadan.

These two reports are not to be used to oppose the earlier reports, because the earlier reports agree with the apparent meaning of the Qur'an and the mutawatir reports that we mentioned, while these two reports oppose that; so it is not permissible to act upon them. Moreover, in them is that which confirms the view of the invalidity of relying on numerical counting, because if the criterion were the count, then the day in which the الهلال was seen would definitively and firmly be either from Ramadan or from Shawwāl, and there would be no intelligible meaning to its being seen before midday or after midday. Still, it is possible that they may be acted upon in some respects, namely: when the الهلال was not seen in the town at night because they missed its rising place, and it was seen the next day before midday, and to that is joined the testimony of two witnesses from outside the city regarding sighting, then it is permissible to act upon that. And no one may say that with the testimony of the two witnesses there is no consideration for sighting the الهلال before midday; rather, acting upon their testimony is only obligatory when there is in the town some impediment such as cloud, dust, or the like. But with clear skies, the testimony of two persons from outside the town is not accepted; rather, there is need for the testimony of fifty, equal to the number in qasamah. And that which indicates this is: 7. What Saʿd ibn ʿAbdillāh narrated, from Ibrāhīm ibn Hāshim, from Ismāʿīl ibn Marrār, from Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Ḥabīb al-Khuzāʿī, who said: Abū ʿAbdillāh, peace be upon him, said: Testimony regarding sighting the الهلال is not valid with fewer than fifty men, equal to the number in qasamah; and the testimony of two men is only valid when they are from outside the town and there is some impediment in the city, and they report that they saw it and report from people who fasted based on the sighting.

key_terms.الزَّوَالِ: midday; the point after which the sun declines from its zenith
key_terms.الصِّيَامَ: the fast being observed during the day
key_terms.الْقَسَامَةِ: the counted legal number invoked here as a measure of testimony
key_terms.الْهِلَالُ: the new crescent moon by which the lunar month is established
key_terms.شَهَادَةُ: legal testimony used to establish moon sighting
key_terms.شَوَّالٍ: the month following Ramadan, marking the end of the fasting month

ai.seo_question: If the الهلال of Shawwāl is seen during the day in Ramadan, should one break the fast or complete it until night?
ai.summary: This text gathers several hadith on establishing the beginning and end of Ramadan and Shawwāl through sighting the الهلال. Its central ruling is that if the الهلال is only seen during the daytime, one completes the fast until night, while broader discussion addresses the weight of witness testimony and the reconciliation or rejection of apparently conflicting reports.
